test_title: RRB NTPC Graduate Level CBT-I Official Paper (Held On: 05 Jun, 2025 Shift 2)
subject: general
question: Marks in statistics of 12 students are x, 28, 35, 56, 78, 63, 65, 81, 79, 83, 80, y, where x and y are the lowest and highest marks, respectively. If the range and average of the marks are 70 and 64, respectively, then the ordered pair (x, y) is:
solution: __Shortcut Trick__ Sum of **lowest (x)** and **highest (y)** marks = (Average × Total students) − Sum of other 10 marks. x + y = (64 × 12) − 648 = 768 − 648 = 120. Given **Range** (y − x) = 70. Solving: y = (120 + 70) ÷ 2 = 95 and x = (120 − 70) ÷ 2 = 25. **∴ The correct answer is (25 , 95).** **__Alternate Method__** **Given:** Marks of **12 students**, Average = 64, Range = 70, x = lowest, y = highest. **Formula Used:** Average = Sum ÷ Count | Range = Highest − Lowest [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/135b31fb26238b35f1cc2c3a928fd68538b3fe7fb7d3c71342a98f38f0165e0d.png] ⇒ Sum of all 12 marks = 12 × 64 = 768 ⇒ Sum of known 10 marks = 28 + 35 + 56 + 78 + 63 + 65 + 81 + 79 + 83 + 80 = 648 ⇒ x + y = 768 − 648 = 120 ⇒ y − x = 70 (Given Range) ⇒ Adding both: 2y = 190 ⇒ y = 95 ⇒ Subtracting: 2x = 50 ⇒ x = 25 **∴ The correct answer is (25 , 95).** **__Additional Information__** Range in Statistics
